meta.move: Written by the lead after attempt 1 (not blind): owns the zero, shows each piece by saying so, answers each defence in a sentence, offers 4.4, sets a date
meta.expect: She reaches the deal after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Who decided to give my son a zero before anyone called me?
Thanks for coming in. Before anything else: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. That was wrong, and Owen shouldn't have found out on his phone.
Okay. Now show me what you have on the essay.

I've turned my laptop to you. This is the document's version history: created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. No earlier drafts.
11:52, 11:58. People write somewhere else and paste it in, Hale.
If he drafted it somewhere else, he can bring that draft with its date and I'll look at it. Until then, this record is what we have.
Whatever comes of this, it stays off his record, and it stays quiet. What else do you have?
Here's the essay, page two, and here's the play open to Act 3, Scene 2. The essay quotes 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' Search the scene yourself; it isn't there.
A misquote is a careless kid, not a cheating one.
A misquote from memory is usually close to a real line. This one isn't close to anything in the play.
Then tell me exactly what you want from Owen, and what it costs him.
Here's his October 15 outline beside the essay. The outline argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice.
Kids change their argument after an outline, Hale. That's the point of one.

Here's what I can offer under procedure 4.4: a private supervised rewrite, after school, not in front of his class, before December 1. The new mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.
To put this behind him, yes. Private, before December 1, nothing on file, and in my inbox tonight.
Thursday the twelfth after school works for me. Does that work for Owen?
I'll check his shifts tonight and confirm by email.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Dear Hale,

In today's meeting you agreed that Owen will complete a private supervised rewrite after school, not in front of his class, that its mark will replace the zero, and that nothing will be placed on his record. I still require that commitment in writing, along with a confirmed date that fits Owen's work schedule. I expect your written confirmation tonight, and the rewrite completed before December 1.

Meredith Kalinowski
cc: Principal, Elbow Crossing High School

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She reached her last position and agreed to a private supervised rewrite to put this behind him; she still wants your written promise tonight that nothing goes on his record and a date that fits his shifts, and that is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4.
What moved her: Opening with a one-sentence apology for entering the zero before calling home, then showing the version history with its exact times, gave her something dated and tied to Owen's own document that she could check herself.
What cost ground: Nothing; you never leaned on the detector score, never called Owen a liar, and answered her paste-from-elsewhere defence with a fair, checkable request.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history put the whole essay between 11:31 and 11:58 on a late October night, very close to that memory. It proves nothing about the essay; it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she said kids change their argument after an outline, answer that point directly before offering 4.4, for example by noting that the version history shows the new argument arriving in two large edits with no draft in between.
